## Description

`npx skills update <skill-name>` silently fails on Windows when `process.execPath` contains spaces (e.g. `C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe`).

The command outputs `✗ Failed to update <skill-name>` with no further details.

## Root Cause

In `updateProjectSkills` (and `updateGlobalSkills`), the update spawns a subprocess like this:

```js
spawnSync(process.execPath, [cliEntry, "add", installUrl, "-y"], {
  shell: process.platform === "win32"
});
```

On Windows, `shell: true` causes the command to be executed via `cmd.exe`. Since `process.execPath` is not quoted, `cmd.exe` break
items.title: [Bug] skills update fails on Windows when Node.js path contains spaces

items.author: benedictkwok
items.body:
Summary
python
`process = subprocess.Popen(
    server['cmd'],
    shell=True,
    stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
    stderr=subprocess.PIPE
)
`
server['cmd'] is taken directly from the --server CLI argument (argparse, action='append', no validation) and passed to subprocess.Popen(..., shell=True) with no sanitization. Any shell metacharacters in the value (;, &&, $(), backticks, etc.) are interpreted by /bin/sh.

Why this one is more than theoretical?

Per the script's own usage docs (lines 5–14), this is meant to be invoked as part of automated test workflows: python scripts/with_server.py --server
items.title: Shell command injection via --server argument (with_server.py, shell=True)  Affected file: webapp-testing/scripts/with_server.py (lines 69–74)
